title: Two Proud Goats
summary: Two goats meet in the middle of a narrow bridge over a river, and neither one is willing to give way. A fable about stubbornness and pride.
pages: In a village there was a narrow bridge over the river. Only one could cross it at a time.
Once, a goat started to cross the bridge. Then another goat came from the other side, onto the same bridge.
They stood face to face, right in the middle of the bridge. One goat said angrily, "Let me cross first!" The other answered, "I've already walked so far, you go back. Let me cross first!"
Both of them were stubborn and wouldn't give in. Then they got tangled up with each other, because both goats were foolish.
And so they both fell into the river and drowned. The moral: whoever is foolishly stubborn only harms himself.
